messages:
alex: Kickoff: proposing a 'heterogeneous-quant-fallback' pattern for model bring-ups that use mixed int4/int8 mappings. Goal: graceful degradation that prefers per-customer routing and tiered fallback instead of full auto-rollback.

mei: sounds promising. What's the main difference vs our existing soft-fail/auto-fallback?

alex: two differences: (1) fallback is graduated by capability (int8 fallback, then quantized-v2, then baseline), and (2) fallback decisions consider customer tier and in-flight SLA exposure. So enterprise customers could get auto-route to baseline while best-effort ones see int8 fallback.

priya: nice. Can you sketch the decision tree? Also we should attach a short-circuit for hard safety signals (e.g., hallucination spike) to bypass graduated steps.

alex: draft decision logic below. We'll emit full telemetry tags so ops can see why a route was changed.

```yaml
heterogeneous_quant_fallback:
  signals: [fidelity_pct_drop, mrr_delta, hallucination_rate, p95_latency]
  hard_abort_conditions:
    hallucination_rate: 3.0   # absolute pct -> immediate baseline route for all
  graduated_steps:
    - name: int8_fallback
      description: fall back to int8 mapped weights
      conditions: [fidelity_pct_drop <= 5%, mrr_delta >= -0.03]
    - name: quantv2_adjust
      description: try alternate int4 mapping (symmetric) with layer exceptions
      conditions: [fidelity_pct_drop <= 8%]
    - name: full-baseline
      description: route to baseline model (no quant)
  customer_tiers:
    enterprise: prefer_immediate_baseline=true
    standard: prefer_graduated=true
  telemetry_tags_to_emit: [fallback_step, reason_vector, customer_tier, slice_weights]
  cooldown_minutes: 120
```

mei: implementation note: rollout controller should publish `fallback_step` and `reason_vector` and mark the event with model_hash + quant_config so triage can diff weights.

ops-bot: simulation summary for run_id=99121 (mixed-quant candidate):
```
samples=15k, slices={short:50%, longform:30%, dialogue:20%}
signals:\n  fidelity_pct_drop: 4.6\n  mrr_delta: -0.018\n  hallucination_rate: 0.9\n  p95_latency: +22ms
initial_decision: qualifies for int8_fallback per conditions -> route int8 for standard customers, baseline for enterprise
actions: emit telemetry tags fallback_step=int8_fallback, reason_vector=[fidelity,mrr]
```

priya: good. For longform slice we still see a 6.5% fidelity drop but it's concentrated in long prefixes. Suggest targeted expedites: (1) longform annotated rerun 8k samples, (2) run token-level alignment, (3) short-circuit to baseline for enterprise before widespread promote.

alex: agree. Also propose a metric-weight cap: if any single slice weighted impact >10% of user impressions and fidelity_drop>5% then move ahead one fallback step immediately. That prevents exposure from heavy slices.

eval-bot: actual canary run id=99121a deployed at 5% for 30m -> report:
```
aggregate_fidelity_drop: 4.9
longform_fidelity_drop: 6.5 (weight 30%)
mrr_delta: -0.02
hallucination_rate: 1.1
decision: int8_fallback triggered for standard customers; enterprise routed to baseline. Cooldown engaged. Ticket created: TKT-5020
```

release-owner: I'll own enterprise communications. Can we make the per-customer routing pluggable per-tenant flag? Some enterprise customers may accept int8 if they opt-in.

mei: yes add a tenant flag `allow_degraded_quant` with default false. Also add audit log entry for any automated routing change.

priya: ops follow-up: ensure the chain of custody for fallback decisions is recorded (who acked, which thresholds triggered, snapshot of telemetry at trigger). This helps when we reconcile customer complaints.

alex: action items: (1) mei -> rollout-service PR to implement fallback_step tag + per-tenant routing, (2) priya -> run longform annotated rerun and post results, (3) eval-bot -> simulate int8 vs quantv2 for targeted slice. I'll draft gatebook entry "heterogeneous-quant-fallback" with decision tree and playbook.

ops-bot: note: enforce minimum dwell 10m per step and ensure model hash + quant mapping are immutable in event logs.

eval-bot: t+12h snapshot: longform annotated rerun showed hallucination parity restored after int8 fallback; candidate int4v2 reduced longform fidelity drop to 2.1% in a focused re-run; recommendation: merge quantv2 mapping and run a controlled 10% promote with consensus gate enabled.

alex: excellent. closing thread once PR is merged and gatebook entry live. Thanks all. :rocket:
